analysis:
Examined three changed files; no regression is supported by the supplied evidence.

1) ProviderLoop+StartupPreload.swift head 299-305: finishStartupPreload now queues skipped-for-memory, failed-for-memory and not-attempted candidates for selected-model recovery. It does so only when the task is not cancelled, shutdown has not begun and no stall-stop was requested. Self-test-retired models are not queued, because summary.retired/selfTestFailed are excluded. The recovery implementation (ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery) was not supplied. Integration must confirm three things: it loads with allowEviction:false; it honours advertisedModels, isRefusedByRetirement and failedSelfTestHashes (head 421-480), so a fail-closed build is never re-advertised; and it is cancelled on shutdown and serving drain. Shutdown is also guarded by the load-install guard noted at StartupShutdown head 36-38. This is availability/T-029-adjacent with no direct A-001 exposure.

2) ProviderLoop+StartupShutdown.swift head 60, 77-96 and 99-107: the unbounded unload loop (base 60-68) is replaced by a 15s per-slot bounded wait. Slots whose unload does not finish are abandoned and the function returns true, relying on process exit. Order is unchanged: stopAppAttestWorkerAndWait, inflight drain/cancel, coordinator shutdown and drainNativeMiMoOwners all still precede unloading. Credential custody (A-008/T-053) and App Attest teardown are therefore not affected. Two edge cases remain:
- An abandoned unload Task may still run after the function returns, alongside the clearCache at head 62. This is a stability concern, not a confidentiality one.
- Abandoned slots keep decrypted KV/weights in memory until exit. This is the same residency already covered by T-028/T-014.

3) ProviderLoop+Testing.swift head 514-525: new internal test seams for the recovery load override and for awaiting a recovery attempt. They are not #if DEBUG, consistent with existing seams. They are internal-only and add no external surface.

No change was found to encryption, attestation, routing authorization, cache (T-041) or billing paths.
